lessons.titleZh: 面對外來壓力時團結防守

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The residents close ranks after an emergency.
sources.expression: close ranks

brief.meaningEn: Unite as a group to defend or support its members in response to an outside challenge.
brief.meaningZh: 面對外來挑戰時，群體團結起來保護或支持成員。
brief.grammar: close ranks around/behind someone; closed/closing; can be supportive or can imply resistance to scrutiny, depending on context
brief.boundaryZh: 不必指字面列隊，也不表示成員所有意見相同；團結回應不自動代表正確或可拒聽合理問題。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不必指字面列隊，也不表示成員所有意見相同；團結回應不自動代表正確或可拒聽合理問題。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「面對外來壓力時團結防守」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: When outside comments blamed the whole volunteer team for one delayed delivery, the members closed ranks to explain the shared record, while still agreeing to review what had caused the delay.
listening.zh: 外界因一次送貨延誤責怪整個義工隊時，成員團結防守，解釋共同紀錄，同時仍同意檢視延誤原因。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 成員共同回應外界責怪，仍願檢視實際問題。
成員互相公開指責，沒有共同回應。
隊伍已拒絕看任何延誤紀錄或回答問題。
共同回應是批評出現前已排的例行宣布，而非對批評作反應。

listening.explanationZh: when outside comments 交代外壓觸發，closed ranks 共同回應且still review，不是先前例行宣布或拒看問題。

reply.promptEn: How did the volunteers respond to the outside criticism?
reply.promptZh: 義工怎回應外界批評？

options.en: They closed ranks to explain the record while agreeing to review the delay.
options.zh: 他們團結防守，解釋紀錄並同意檢視延誤。

options.en: They made a shared response rather than blame one another publicly.
options.zh: 他們共同回應，而非公開互相責怪。

options.en: They defended the team without saying the delivery problem should be ignored.
options.zh: 他們保護團隊，卻沒說應忽略送貨問題。

options.en: The members stood together and still left room for a practical review.
options.zh: 成員站在一起，仍留實際檢視空間。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 一間學會被外人把成員意見斷章取義，委員共同說明完整說法，也邀提問；你想說面對外壓團結，不說因此已免責。哪句貼切？

options.en: The committee closed ranks in response to the misleading account, while inviting questions.
options.zh: 委員面對誤導敘述團結防守，同時邀提問。

options.en: The members split into separate public accusations rather than give a shared account.
options.zh: 成員分成各自公開指責，而非共同交代。

options.en: The invitation to ask questions means they have refused to make any defence of the members.
options.zh: 邀提問表示他們拒絕為成員作任何辯護。

scene.explanationZh: 共同說明是團結回應，邀問可並存，不是互指或全無辯護。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 closed ranks 單獨得出？

options.en: 群體面對挑戰時團結起來。
團結一方在實質問題上必然正確。
上下文可顯示是合理支持還是拒絕檢視。

contrast.explanationZh: 是否團結與立場有否根據是不同問題。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然站在一起，就不應再檢視延誤吧？」隊伍也想知道原因。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: We can close ranks against unfair blame and still examine the actual delay.
options.zh: 我們可面對不公平責怪團結防守，仍檢視實際延誤。

options.en: Use the shared defence as a reason to leave the delivery records unread.
options.zh: 用共同防守作理由，不讀送貨紀錄。

options.en: Avoid a common response until every member has exactly the same view of the cause.
options.zh: 等每位成員對原因看法完全相同，才作共同回應。

dialogue.explanationZh: 共同回應不取消實際檢視，也不需所有因果看法先完全相同。

speaking.en: The group closed ranks when challenged, but that unity did not settle whether every criticism was fair.
speaking.zh: 群體受挑戰時團結防守，但團結不會定每項批評是否公平。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清團結狀態與實質是非。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說評論，一家人因外面謠言團結保護成員，但後來把一位孩子合理的疑問也一併拒聽。你想描述他們 close ranks 的動作，並區別保護與拒絕檢視，不把團結一律說好或壞。用一至兩句英文評述。

examples.en: The family closed ranks against the rumour, but then extended that defence to shutting out the child’s reasonable question. I would distinguish their wish to protect one another from their refusal to listen.
examples.zh: 一家面對謠言團結防守，後來卻把防守擴至拒聽孩子合理問題。我會區分想保護彼此與拒聽。

examples.en: They close ranks when the outside story threatens a family member, which explains the shared response. It does not by itself justify ignoring the child’s separate concern.
examples.zh: 外界故事威脅家人時，他們團結防守，這解釋共同回應；但本身不能合理化忽略孩子另一顧慮。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明外壓下團結及後來過度拒聽的差別，用故事行為評價，不因有團結就先定立場全對或全錯。

takeaways.en: The colleagues closed ranks when the criticism targeted the whole group rather than the disputed decision.
takeaways.zh: 批評針對整組而非有爭議決定時，同事團結防守。

takeaways.en: They could close ranks in support of a member and still ask what evidence the complaint contained.
takeaways.zh: 他們可團結支持成員，仍問投訴有何證據。

lessons.titleZh: 當困難找上門

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: When trouble knocks, neighbours help each other.
sources.expression: when trouble knocks

brief.meaningEn: When a difficulty arrives or makes itself felt, using the image of a visitor at the door.
brief.meaningZh: 以訪客敲門作意象，指困難出現或開始影響生活。
brief.grammar: when trouble knocks, + response; trouble is personified; does not require someone literally at a door. Knocked is the past form in when trouble knocked.
brief.boundaryZh: 未說困難必巨大、是誰的錯或已造成終局；需交代實際問題及可見回應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 未說困難必巨大、是誰的錯或已造成終局；需交代實際問題及可見回應。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「當困難找上門」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: When trouble knocks, our small group usually begins by asking what changed; last week the meeting room became unavailable, so we checked another place before telling members where to go.
listening.zh: 困難找上門時，我們小組通常先問改了甚麼；上周會議房不能用，所以先核另一地方，再通知成員去哪。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 出現場地問題，小組先弄清並核替代。
小組先傳另一地址給成員，之後才查那地方是否可用。
原房間仍可用，小組沒有遇到任何改動。
所有成員已在原房間開完會，之後才知改地點。

listening.explanationZh: checked before telling 先核替代再通知；room became unavailable 是具體困難，不是先傳再查或仍可用。

reply.promptEn: What did the group do when the room became unavailable?
reply.promptZh: 房間不能用時，小組怎做？

options.en: When trouble knocks, we check what changed; that time we looked for another place before giving directions.
options.zh: 困難找上門時，我們先查改了甚麼；那次先找另一地方，才給路線。

options.en: We checked an alternative before telling members where to meet.
options.zh: 通知成員在哪聚前，我們先核替代。

options.en: The immediate problem led us to clarify the new arrangement.
options.zh: 眼前問題令我們先說清新安排。

options.en: We responded to the lost room rather than send people to an unchecked location.
options.zh: 我們回應房間不能用，而非把人送到未核地點。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 故事人物的印表機在準備小刊時停了，朋友先問哪些頁急用，再幫找可用印本；作者用訪客比喻困難出現。哪句貼切？

options.en: When trouble knocks, the friends begin by finding out what help is actually needed.
options.zh: 困難找上門時，朋友先查實際需甚麼幫助。

options.en: The problem is described as solved before anyone asks which pages are needed.
options.zh: 有人問哪些頁需要前，問題已被描述為解決。

options.en: The friends are revising a disputed paragraph while the printer continues to work normally.
options.zh: 朋友在改有爭議段落，而印表機仍正常工作。

scene.explanationZh: 問題是印製停了，朋友先問急用頁，不是內容分歧且印機正常，也不是未問已解決。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 when trouble knocks 得出？

options.en: 在困難出現或影響事情的時候。
困難本身已證人物故意做錯事。
上下文仍需說清是哪項問題。

contrast.explanationZh: trouble 的出現不自帶故意犯錯原因。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「要先問改了甚麼太慢，先傳另一個未核地址吧？」小組仍不知可用地點。哪句回應最合適？

options.en: When trouble knocks, a clear first step matters; let us confirm the place before sending everyone there.
options.zh: 困難找上門時，清楚第一步重要；先確認地方再叫大家去。

options.en: Choose the most familiar address and announce it before asking whether it is open.
options.zh: 先選最熟地址宣布，才問是否開放。

options.en: Send members to the original room because changing a message would be inconvenient.
options.zh: 改訊息麻煩，所以仍叫成員去原房。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先確認實際可用地方，再通知，不以熟悉或省事代查。

speaking.en: When trouble knocks, I would rather ask what is needed than assume I already know the whole answer.
speaking.zh: 困難找上門時，我寧願先問需要甚麼，而不假定已知全部答案。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出具體困難與回應。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想感謝朋友上周在你遇突發行程改動時，沒責怪也沒替你全決定，而是問你最急需接回哪件物品，再幫送到約好地方。你想用困難找上門的比喻珍惜這種先問需要的支持。用一至兩句英文寫謝卡。

examples.en: When trouble knocks, it helps to have someone who asks what is actually needed. Thank you for checking which bag I needed most and bringing it to the place we agreed last week.
examples.zh: 困難找上門時，有人先問實際需要很有幫助。謝謝你上周問我最需哪個袋，再送到議好地方。

examples.en: I appreciated your calm help when trouble knocked last week and my plans suddenly changed. You asked before acting, and getting that bag back made the next step easier.
examples.zh: 上周困難找上門、計劃突改時，我珍惜你冷靜幫助。你先問再行動，拿回那個袋令下一步較易。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以突發改行程作困難例子，具體感謝先問需要及送袋，不把比喻當對方一定要解決全部事情。

takeaways.en: When trouble knocks, neighbours sometimes begin with one small offer that fits the person’s immediate need.
takeaways.zh: 困難找上門時，鄰居有時先提出一個配合當事人眼前需要的小幫助。

takeaways.en: We saw how the team responded when trouble knocked and the usual plan no longer worked.
takeaways.zh: 困難找上門、原計劃不再可行時，我們看見團隊怎回應。

lessons.titleEn: does not make a big noise
lessons.titleZh: 低調發生，不刻意引人注意

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Much local kindness does not make a big noise.
sources.expression: does not make a big noise

brief.meaningEn: Happen or have an effect without much publicity or fuss.
brief.meaningZh: 沒有很多宣傳或張揚，卻仍發生或產生作用。
brief.grammar: quiet help does not make a big noise; abstract help is personified; literal loudness is not the focus of these contexts
brief.boundaryZh: 不張揚不代表沒有作用、秘密行為或所有人完全不知道；需交代實際行動與受幫者反應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不張揚不代表沒有作用、秘密行為或所有人完全不知道；需交代實際行動與受幫者反應。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「低調發生，不刻意引人注意」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Creative sound/publicity metaphor in the supplied kindness sentence, not a claim that every literal use of make a noise has this meaning.

listening.en: The help did not make a big noise: a neighbour quietly replaced the unclear collection note with one everyone could follow, and the next morning people found the right place without another public announcement.
listening.zh: 幫忙沒有張揚：鄰居低調把不清的取物便條換成大家能跟的版本，翌晨大家無需另一次公開宣布便找到正確地方。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 沒有張揚的實際改動，仍幫人找到正確地方。
鄰居沒有改任何資訊，只舉行公開慶祝。
新便條只有寫字的人能理解，其他人仍找不到地方。
幫忙已在大型宣傳中逐項介紹給全場。

listening.explanationZh: quietly replaced 與找到地方支持低調而有用，不是沒有行動或大宣傳。

reply.promptEn: Why did you value that small change to the note?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼珍惜便條那小改動？

options.en: It did not make a big noise, but it helped people find the right place.
options.zh: 它沒有張揚，卻幫大家找到正確地方。

options.en: The neighbour made the instructions usable without turning it into a public event.
options.zh: 鄰居讓指示可用，沒把它變公開活動。

options.en: People could follow the new note the next morning.
options.zh: 翌晨大家可跟新便條。

options.en: Its value lay in the practical effect, not in an announcement about the helper.
options.zh: 它的價值在實際作用，不在介紹幫忙者的宣布。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 同伴每次為缺席會議的人整理決定及尚未解決的問題，私下傳去，不宣傳自己多做；對方說可據此補上意見。你想描述低調卻有作用的照顧。哪句貼切？

options.en: The care does not make a big noise, but the absent member can use the notes to take part.
options.zh: 照顧沒有張揚，但缺席成員可用筆記參與。

options.en: The notes are mainly an announcement praising the writer, rather than a record the absent member can use.
options.zh: 筆記主要是讚作者的公告，而非缺席者可用的記錄。

options.en: The notes leave out the open questions, so the absent member is told there is nothing left to contribute.
options.zh: 筆記不提未決問題，告訴缺席者已沒可補充之處。

scene.explanationZh: 整理決定及未決問題、令對方可補意見，是低調實用支持，不是自我宣傳或關閉參與。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由此處 does not make a big noise 得出？

options.en: 沒有刻意張揚或很多宣傳。
行動沒有實際作用，沒有人可能從中受益。
需由實際回應看低調行動帶來甚麼幫助。

contrast.explanationZh: 低調不等於無效。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「沒公開宣布，就沒甚麼值得記吧？」便條確幫大家找到地方。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: It did not make a big noise, but the practical help is still worth describing.
options.zh: 它沒有張揚，但實際幫助仍值得描述。

options.en: Include only the large announcements when deciding what helped people.
options.zh: 判甚麼有幫時，只包括大型宣布。

options.en: Measure the note only by how often the helper’s name was repeated.
options.zh: 只按幫忙者名字重複多少次評便條。

dialogue.explanationZh: 實際改動可有價值，不需由公開聲量或名字次數證明。

speaking.en: The kindness does not make a big noise, but its practical effect matters to the people receiving it.
speaking.zh: 善意沒有張揚，但實際作用對受幫者重要。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清不張揚與沒有作用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為社團服務獎提名一位同伴，他常替初次來的人核清路線、問是否需大字版資料，沒有公開介紹自己。你想向評審具體說低調工作為何值得肯定，不用掌聲多少來證價值。用一至兩句英文寫提名理由。

examples.en: His help does not make a big noise, but first-time visitors can find their way and ask for readable information because of it. I would recognise those quiet, repeated contributions in the service award.
examples.zh: 他的幫助沒有張揚，但初訪者因此能找路、提出可讀資料需要。我會在服務獎肯定這些低調反覆貢獻。

examples.en: The care does not make a big noise; he checks routes and information needs without making himself the centre of the visit. Those practical details are why I am nominating him.
examples.zh: 照顧沒有張揚；他核路線及資訊需要，不把自己變參觀中心。那些實際細節是我提名他的理由。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以可找路及資料需要的具體支持提名，尊重低調而非認定無人受惠，不用公開聲量代作用。

takeaways.en: The support did not make a big noise, but it helped a new member feel less lost.
takeaways.zh: 支持沒有張揚，但幫新人沒那麼迷惘。

takeaways.en: Their everyday care does not make a big noise, so the report includes the small changes people actually noticed.
takeaways.zh: 他們日常照顧沒有張揚，所以報告包括大家實際留意的小改動。

lessons.titleEn: the world does not revolve around them
lessons.titleZh: 世界不是只圍着某人轉

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Children need to learn that the world does not revolve around them.
sources.expression: the world does not revolve around them

brief.meaningEn: Other people’s needs and perspectives matter too; one person is not the centre of everything.
brief.meaningZh: 別人的需要及觀點同樣重要，不能只以一個人作中心。
brief.grammar: the world does not revolve around you/them; did not in past; figurative self-centredness criticism, not astronomy
brief.boundaryZh: 提醒考慮別人，不是說當事人沒有價值或不能表達需要；要看具體忽略了誰，而不全盤定人格。
brief.misconceptionZh: 提醒考慮別人，不是說當事人沒有價值或不能表達需要；要看具體忽略了誰，而不全盤定人格。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「世界不是只圍着某人轉」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: He wanted every rehearsal moved to suit his own train, until the others explained their caring duties and work hours; the world did not revolve around him, and the next plan needed to include those constraints too.
listening.zh: 他想每次排練都改來配合自己的火車，直到別人解釋照顧責任及工作時間；世界不是只圍他轉，下個計劃也需包括那些限制。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 安排需顧其他人的限制，不只一人交通。
別人的需要表示他不再可以提自己的火車時間。
小組已選擇只按他的時間，不計其他人。
各人的限制其實相同，沒有任何不同需要。

listening.explanationZh: too 要納別人需要，不是抹去他的或假定所有人相同。

reply.promptEn: Why did the rehearsal plan need another discussion?
reply.promptZh: 排練計劃為甚麼需再談？

options.en: The world did not revolve around him; other people’s duties and work hours mattered too.
options.zh: 世界不是只圍他轉；別人照顧責任及工時也重要。

options.en: His train was not the only constraint on the group’s time.
options.zh: 他的火車不是小組時間唯一限制。

options.en: The plan had to include needs he had not yet considered.
options.zh: 計劃需包括他尚未考慮的需要。

options.en: Everyone needed a chance to explain what they could manage.
options.zh: 每人都需機會解釋可應付甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物想旅行每站都只看自己喜歡的展品，沒問同伴步行時間及想休息多久；現在同伴請一起議路線。哪句貼切？

options.en: She needs to remember that the world does not revolve around her when they plan the day.
options.zh: 計劃一天時，她需記得世界不是只圍她轉。

options.en: Asking the others means she must never mention her own interests again.
options.zh: 問別人表示她不能再提自己的興趣。

options.en: Only the person who first suggested the trip should have a view on the route.
options.zh: 只有最初提議旅行的人才應對路線有看法。

scene.explanationZh: 共同議定是納各人需要，不是抹去自己或只讓一人有意見。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 the world does not revolve around them 得出？

options.en: 別人的需要也要被考慮。
他們自己的需要完全沒有價值。
可用具體共同安排解釋為何不能只顧一人。

contrast.explanationZh: 不獨佔中心不等於無價值。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然不只顧我，我就不應提火車時間吧？」大家仍需知他的限制。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: The world does not revolve around you, but your needs still belong in a discussion that includes everyone else’s.
options.zh: 世界不是只圍你轉，但你的需要仍屬包括其他人的討論一部分。

options.en: Leave your travel needs out so the others can make a plan without that information.
options.zh: 不提你的交通需要，讓其他人沒那資料作計劃。

options.en: Give your train priority before asking whether the others have caring duties.
options.zh: 未問別人是否有照顧責任，就先讓你的火車優先。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需一併納各人限制，不是只顧自己或完全刪自己的資料。

speaking.en: The world does not revolve around me, but I can explain my needs while making room for yours too.
speaking.zh: 世界不是只圍我轉，但我可解釋需要，也為你的需要留空間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清不獨佔中心與沒有價值。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與朋友合寫故事，自己未問便刪掉他最重視的結尾，只因不合你想法。現在想道歉，承認不能只以自己作中心，請他解釋結尾想保留甚麼，再一起改；不是說你從此不能提意見。用一至兩句英文發訊息。

examples.en: I need to remember that the world does not revolve around me; I cut your ending before asking why it mattered to you. I am sorry, and I would like us to discuss what each of us wants to keep.
examples.zh: 我需記得世界不是只圍我轉；我未問為何重要就刪了你的結尾。對不起，我想一起談各人想保留甚麼。

examples.en: The world does not revolve around me, and my preferred ending should not have been the only one considered. Could you explain what you want the final scene to do before we revise it together?
examples.zh: 世界不是只圍我轉，我偏好的結尾不應是唯一被考慮的。一起改前，可否解釋你想最後一幕達到甚麼？

glossary.en: what each of us wants to keep

writing.selfCheckZh: 為未問便刪對方結尾作具體道歉，邀聽雙方目的及共同修改，不把不獨佔中心變自己不可再有意見。

takeaways.en: She realised the world did not revolve around her when she heard why the others needed a different meeting time.
takeaways.zh: 聽到別人需另一會議時間的原因後，她明白世界不是只圍她轉。

takeaways.en: The world does not revolve around us, so we should ask how our plan affects the people sharing the space.
takeaways.zh: 世界不是只圍我們轉，所以應問計劃怎影響共用空間的人。

lessons.titleEn: look up, look around, and step outside themselves
lessons.titleZh: 抬頭看看周圍，走出自我關注

target.pattern: \blook up,? look around,? and step outside (?:ourselves|themselves|yourself|yourselves|myself|himself|herself)\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Volunteering teaches children to look up, look around, and step outside themselves.
sources.expression: look up, look around, and step outside themselves

brief.meaningEn: Notice the people around oneself and consider needs beyond one’s own immediate concerns.
brief.meaningZh: 留意身邊的人，考慮自己眼前關注以外的需要。
brief.grammar: learn to look up, look around, and step outside ourselves; coordinated invitation, with outside-oneself perspective metaphor
brief.boundaryZh: 不是身體真的走到自己外面，也不要求忽略自己需要；要具體指出看見誰及怎改觀點或行動。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是身體真的走到自己外面，也不要求忽略自己需要；要具體指出看見誰及怎改觀點或行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「抬頭看看周圍，走出自我關注」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: A deliberately rhythmic cluster combining noticing and a perspective metaphor, not one fixed dictionary idiom. Learner pronouns match the viewpoint while exact source wording remains in provenance.

listening.en: Helping at the book fair taught us to look up, look around, and step outside ourselves: instead of thinking only about our own display, we noticed visitors who could not find a place to ask a question.
listening.zh: 書展幫忙教我們抬頭看看周圍、走出自我關注：不只想自己的展示，也留意找不到地方提問的訪客。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 注意由自己展示擴到訪客的實際需要。
大家不再可關心自己的作品或準備。
訪客已全問完問題，沒有任何需留意的情況。
主要目的是比較誰的展示得到最多掌聲。

listening.explanationZh: instead of only 展示觀點擴大而非刪自己，noticing visitors 給具體對象。

reply.promptEn: How did volunteering change what you paid attention to?
reply.promptZh: 義工經驗怎改變你們留意的事情？

options.en: It helped us look up, look around, and step outside ourselves to notice visitors who needed a place to ask.
options.zh: 它幫我們抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注，留意需地方提問的訪客。

options.en: We began considering more than our own display.
options.zh: 我們開始考慮不只自己展示。

options.en: The visitors’ experience became part of what we watched for.
options.zh: 訪客經驗成為我們留意的一部分。

options.en: We noticed a practical need we had missed while focusing on our own work.
options.zh: 我們留意到原專注自己作品時漏掉的實際需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 小組想為新會員辦活動，原只列自己喜歡的項目；後來先聽新人怕不知找誰、想有短介紹的需要。哪句貼切？

options.en: We need to look up, look around, and step outside ourselves when planning for the newcomers.
options.zh: 為新人計劃時，我們需抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注。

options.en: Only the organisers’ favourite activities should guide what newcomers are offered.
options.zh: 只應按主辦者最愛活動，決定供新人甚麼。

options.en: Listening to newcomers means the organisers cannot mention their own experience at all.
options.zh: 聽新人表示主辦者完全不能提自己經驗。

scene.explanationZh: 考慮新人擴大角度，不是只顧自己或禁自己聲音。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 look up, look around, and step outside themselves 得出？

options.en: 擴闊注意及觀點，留意別人。
必須否定及忽略自己所有需要。
需交代因看見別人而有甚麼具體理解或改動。

contrast.explanationZh: 走出自我關注不是抹去自我。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「想別人，就不能再問自己的展示需求吧？」你只是想同時看訪客。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: We can look up, look around, and step outside ourselves without pretending our own needs do not exist.
options.zh: 我們可抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注，而不假裝自己沒有需要。

options.en: Keep the visitors’ difficulties out of the planning so the display remains our only concern.
options.zh: 計劃不提訪客困難，令自己展示仍是唯一關注。

options.en: Remove all the organisers’ practical questions instead of hearing both sets of needs.
options.zh: 不聽雙方需要，直接刪主辦者所有實際問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應一併納多方需要，不是唯一自己或完全無自己。

speaking.en: We need to look up, look around, and step outside ourselves to understand how the plan feels to the people arriving for the first time.
speaking.zh: 我們需抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注，理解計劃對首次來的人是甚麼感受。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再找出自我以外的具體觀點。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與同伴想把屋苑空地改成只供自己年齡層的活動角，卻未問帶小孩、長者或夜班住戶。你想發會前訊息，邀先分別聽他們怎用空間，再帶自己的想法一起討論，不假定任何群體偏好。用一至兩句英文提議。

examples.en: We should look up, look around, and step outside ourselves before deciding how the shared space will be used. Could we hear from families, older residents and night workers as well as bring our own ideas?
examples.zh: 決定共用空間用途前，我們應抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注。可否聽家庭、長者及夜班住戶，也帶自己的想法？

examples.en: Let us look up, look around, and step outside ourselves by asking different residents about their actual use of the space. We can put our proposal beside those needs rather than assume it suits everyone.
examples.zh: 我們問不同住戶實際怎用空間，抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注。可把自己的提案與那些需要並列，而非假定合人人。

writing.selfCheckZh: 邀實際聽多方而非代群體假定，保留自己提案可加入比較，不把注意別人變完全放棄自己。

takeaways.en: The visit encouraged us to look up, look around, and step outside ourselves before judging what the neighbourhood needed.
takeaways.zh: 參觀鼓勵我們先抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注，再判鄰里需甚麼。

takeaways.en: They learned to look up, look around, and step outside themselves when listening to people whose days were different from theirs.
takeaways.zh: 聽日常不同的人時，他們學着抬頭看周圍、走出自我關注。

lessons.titleEn: leave a long shadow in a good way
lessons.titleZh: 留下長久的正面影響

target.pattern: \bleave(?:s|ing)? a long shadow,? in a good way\b|\bleft a long shadow,? in a good way\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A kind lesson can leave a long shadow in a good way.
sources.expression: leave a long shadow in a good way

brief.meaningEn: Have a lasting positive influence, with an explicit qualifier reversing the often negative shadow image.
brief.meaningZh: 留下長久正面影響；以明說好的一面，改變陰影常有的負面聯想。
brief.grammar: an experience can leave a long shadow in a good way; left in past; the qualifier is important to this creative positive use
brief.boundaryZh: 並非慣用語一定正面，需有 in a good way 及具體好影響；長久不等於完全決定後來人生。
brief.misconceptionZh: 並非慣用語一定正面，需有 in a good way 及具體好影響；長久不等於完全決定後來人生。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「留下長久的正面影響」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Creative positive extension of long-shadow influence imagery, not a fixed proverb. Related1742 long shadow behind the present may describe continuing past influence; retain this explicit positive reversal without inventing a separate dictionary sense.

listening.en: The neighbour who first welcomed him had left a long shadow in a good way: years later he still remembered the patient introduction and made sure new arrivals had someone to sit with.
listening.zh: 最初歡迎他的鄰居留下長久正面影響：多年後，他仍記得耐心介紹，也確保新人有人同坐。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 早前受歡迎的經驗，持續影響他後來如何接待新人。
陰影表示那鄰居的行為在敘述中主要帶來恐懼。
他後來的做法與早前經驗完全無關，敘述沒作連接。
說話者只在對比兩位鄰居的社交風格，沒有描述一個人的長久影響。

listening.explanationZh: in a good way、years later remembered 及接待新人，把早前行動與後來好影響相連，不是只作風格比較或主要談恐懼。

reply.promptEn: What lasting influence did the first welcome have?
reply.promptZh: 最初歡迎留下甚麼長久影響？

options.en: It left a long shadow in a good way, shaping how he welcomed newcomers years later.
options.zh: 它留下長久正面影響，塑造他多年後怎歡迎新人。

options.en: He remembered the patient introduction and repeated the care for others.
options.zh: 他記得耐心介紹，再給別人同樣關懷。

options.en: The welcome became a model he returned to in later situations.
options.zh: 歡迎成為他後來回到的榜樣。

options.en: A small early kindness influenced his later habit of including people.
options.zh: 早前小善意，影響他日後接納人的習慣。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 地方工匠當年願教新人並分享方法，搬走多年後，學徒仍沿用那開放態度帶後來的人；作者明說是好影響。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her example left a long shadow in a good way.
options.zh: 她的榜樣留下長久正面影響。

options.en: The account says the apprentices forgot her approach as soon as she left.
options.zh: 敘述說她一離開，學徒便忘了做法。

options.en: The influence is presented mainly as a burden that prevented anyone from learning.
options.zh: 影響主要被寫成阻止任何人學習的負擔。

scene.explanationZh: 多年後仍用開放態度帶人，是持續好影響，不是即忘或負擔。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 leave a long shadow in a good way 得出？

options.en: 明說有長久正面影響。
long shadow 在任何語境都只代表值得稱讚。
需有具體後續，才知好影響如何延續。

contrast.explanationZh: 正面需由 qualifier 及情境支持，不能推所有 shadow 用法都讚。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「shadow 不是常帶負面嗎？這裏怎理解？」後文有多年後接納新人。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: The writer adds “in a good way” and shows the welcome shaping later care, so the shadow is deliberately positive here.
options.zh: 作者加 in a good way，並展示歡迎塑造後來關懷，所以這裏刻意用作正面。

options.en: Ignore the qualifier and describe the later care as fear of the neighbour.
options.zh: 忽略限定語，把後來關懷說成怕鄰居。

options.en: Treat the word shadow alone as proof that every later choice was controlled by the neighbour.
options.zh: 單用 shadow 就當每個後來選擇全受鄰居控制。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需讀明說好及後續行為，不忽略限定或誇成完全控制。

speaking.en: That small act left a long shadow in a good way, influencing how she treated new people years later.
speaking.zh: 那小行動留下長久正面影響，影響她多年後怎待新人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再找正面及長久的具體線索。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為舊樂譜檔案展寫介紹，早年有人免費整理地方曲調，後來不同創作者借它編出自己風格的新作品。你想說這份開放檔案留下長久好影響，但不表示後人只可模仿原版。用一至兩句英文寫展板。

examples.en: The open music archive has left a long shadow in a good way: later composers used the local melodies to create work in their own styles. Its influence lives on through adaptation, not only imitation.
examples.zh: 開放樂譜檔案留下長久正面影響：後來作曲者用地方曲調，創作自己風格作品。影響透過改編延續，不只模仿。

examples.en: Sharing the old scores left a long shadow in a good way, giving new writers material they could reshape. This display follows that continuing influence without treating the original version as the only possible model.
examples.zh: 分享舊樂譜留下長久正面影響，讓新創作者有可重塑材料。這展示追溯持續影響，不把原版當唯一模式。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用後來不同風格作品支持長久好影響，保留明說正面及後人自主，不把影響等同只能模仿或全部受控制。

takeaways.en: The freely shared designs left a long shadow in a good way, giving later makers a starting point for new creations.
takeaways.zh: 免費分享的設計留下長久正面影響，給後來製作者新創作的起點。

takeaways.en: The patient welcome left a long shadow in a good way: years later, he made time for hesitant newcomers before asking them to introduce their work.
takeaways.zh: 那次耐心歡迎留下長久正面影響：多年後，他請猶豫新人介紹作品前，也先為他們留時間。
